input.text: You've just stepped into the Temple of Heaven — and for five hundred years, this is where China's emperors came to speak with the sky itself. Twice a year, the Ming and Qing emperors left the Forbidden City in solemn procession and traveled here to pray for good harvests — for the empire, this was the most important ritual of the year. At the heart of the complex rises the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests: a circular masterpiece of wood, famous for being built without a single nail, standing on three tiers of marble. The circle stood for heaven; the square grounds below, for earth. When UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1998, it called the temple "a masterpiece of architecture and landscape design" that shaped the Far East for centuries. But here's the secret locals know: this is also a park. On weekend mornings, thousands gather — dancing, singing opera, playing chess under ancient cypresses. Stay a while. Heaven can wait.
